subject: Re: Availability commitments, maintenance windows and credit mechanics
messages:
From: Marie Chen <marie.chen@ivorytech.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: SLA redlines and maintenance cadence

Dylan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at IvoryTech asked me to send our proposed SLA redlines so we can lock the commercial terms ahead of the PO. Attached is a PDF with the redlines applied to the Order Form and a short table summarizing the items that are material to us: uptime target, credits, response times for sev1/sev2, and maintenance windows. High-level asks:

- Uptime target: 99.95% (we understand you list 99.9% in the order form; we want parity with our other vendors)
- Service credits: pro-rated by minute with a cap of 25% of monthly fee per calendar month
- Response SLAs: 30 min for P1, 4 hours for P2 for production incidents
- Maintenance: no more than 3 planned maintenance events per quarter; 72-hour advance notice required

Can you confirm these are things Redwood can accept or propose counter-language? We need final Order Form by the end of next week to meet our procurement timeline.

Attachments: IvoryTech_SLA_Redlines_20260525.pdf (redline), redline-diff-orderform.docx (tracked changes)

Thanks,
Marie Chen
Senior Procurement Manager
IvoryTech

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SLA redlines and maintenance cadence

Laura / Grace — forwarding IvoryTech's redlines. Key commercial asks above. My read: these are fairly standard but the uptime + credit cap and the maintenance notice requirements could be friction points.

Suggested internal positions (first pass):
- Uptime: propose 99.9% (standard for Dedicated tier). Offer single-month exception (99.95%) only if customer takes dedicated pool or commits to a 12-month Reserved capacity contract.
- Credits: accept linear credits but cap at 15% of monthly fee; since IvoryTech is asking for 25%, we should push back and propose a 3-month lookback for repeated incidents rather than a high single-month cap.
- Response times: we can agree to 30 min P1 and 4 hrs P2 for production if they accept a dedicated on-call routing / stricter on-call contact details and a recognized P1 definition.
- Maintenance: 72-hour notice is doable for planned updates, but no more than 6 maintenance events per year (instead of 3 per quarter). For emergency security patches we need the ability to do immediate hotfixes with post-facto notice.

Can Legal draft counters and Ops confirm feasibility/impact to cadence and scheduling? I marked two action items below:
1) Laura: please draft the suggested clause language for credits, uptime exceptions, and maintenance (we should be explicit about scheduled vs emergency maintenance).
2) Grace: can you confirm whether 3 planned maintenance events per quarter is operationally feasible and whether a 72-hour notice would block any critical platform updates?

Thanks — I want to respond to Marie by Monday with a single consolidated counterproposal.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 11:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA redlines and maintenance cadence

Dylan / Grace —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed IvoryTech's redlines and prepared proposed clause language below. I attached a short excerpt document (snippets we can insert into the Order Form and MSA). High-level legal position: we should avoid open-ended credit exposure and preserve our right to apply maintenance exclusions and priority tiers. Proposed changes (draft language highlights):

1) Availability Target
"Service Availability" shall mean the percentage of successful request responses measured over a monthly billing cycle. Redwood will use commercially reasonable monitoring to calculate Availability. For the Dedicated plan, Redwood warrants 99.9% monthly Availability. For customers who commit to a minimum twelve (12) month Reserved Capacity contract and provide a named point of contact and required on-call details, Redwood will consider an Availability target of 99.95% subject to separate appendix.

2) Service Credits
If Redwood fails to meet the Availability target in any monthly cycle, Customer may request Service Credits calculated as follows: (a) for each full percentage point below the target, a credit equal to X% of the monthly Service Fees; (b) cumulative credits for a single month shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the monthly Service Fees. Credits are exclusive remedies and shall not entitle customer to termination for convenience. Credits will be issued upon request and after validation by Redwood.

3) Response Times and Severity
Define Severity 1 (P1): production-impacting outage affecting >= X% of requests or causing application unavailability. Redwood will use good faith efforts to respond to P1 within 30 minutes and P2 within four (4) hours during Redwood business hours for Dedicated customers with on-call contact information provided.

4) Maintenance Windows
Planned maintenance shall be scheduled with at least seventy-two (72) hours' advance notice. Redwood shall not perform more than six (6) planned maintenance events per calendar year that impact customer Availability. Emergency maintenance may be performed without prior notice when required to address security vulnerabilities or critical platform integrity issues; in such cases Redwood will provide post-event notice and a remediation summary.

I am attaching redline snippets: "SLA_snippet_redwood_draft_20260527.docx". If Ops confirms the six-per-year cap and the emergency patch carveout works, we can send this as our formal counter. I also kept the credit cap at 15% per month and added language that credits are exclusive and subject to validation — this protects us from downstream termination risk.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_snippet_redwood_draft_20260527.docx

--

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SLA redlines and maintenance cadence

Thanks — operational notes below. TL;DR: Laura's language is workable with a small tweak to planned maintenance frequency and a mechanism for blackout windows for IvoryTech's most critical services.

Operational feasibility: 
- 72-hour notice for planned maintenance: fine for routine platform upgrades and infra housekeeping.
- Frequency: 6 planned events/year is reasonable from our side. We cannot guarantee only 3 events/quarter as IvoryTech requested if they require emergency security hardening or major patching aligned to their release windows.
- Emergency patches: we must retain the ability to do out-of-band patches for security; we'll provide a post-event summary and mitigation steps within 24 hours.

Suggested additions to Laura's draft (ops language):
- Blackout windows: Customer can define up to two recurring 4-hour weekly blackout windows during which Redwood will not schedule planned maintenance that affects Availability. For any requested blackout windows beyond that, Customer and Redwood must agree in writing and adjust the maintenance cadence accordingly.
- Maintenance coordination playbook: Redwood will provide a calendar feed for planned events and an escalation contact list; we will also offer a dedicated maintenance notification distribution list for IvoryTech if they select the Dedicated tier.

Testing impact: if IvoryTech wants 99.95% Availability without Reserved Capacity, we need to run a short operational assessment (2 weeks) to validate traffic patterns and KV cache behavior. If patterns indicate high tail-latency risk, we should require Reserved Capacity to accept the higher SLA.

Action items for reply:
- Laura: finalize the counter language with blackout window and post-event summary SLA (24 hours) for emergency patches.
- Dylan: propose the conditional 99.95% availability language tied to Reserved Capacity / two-week ops assessment.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Marie Chen <marie.chen@ivorytech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA redlines and maintenance cadence

Marie —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity in your asks. We've reviewed internally (Legal + Ops) and we can provide a consolidated counterproposal that preserves your goals while protecting platform operations. Summary of our counter-offer below (see attached redline for exact clause language):

1) Availability: Redwood Dedicated plan standard Availability = 99.9% monthly. We can offer 99.95% as a conditional commitment if IvoryTech either: (a) signs a twelve (12) month Reserved Capacity Order; or (b) completes a two-week operational assessment that validates traffic/latency patterns and infrastructure compatibility. We'll include the conditional language in an appendix.

2) Service Credits: Credits will be available when validated by Redwood; cumulative credits per month will be capped at fifteen percent (15%) of the monthly Service Fees. Credits are exclusive monetary remedies and do not permit termination for convenience.

3) Response Times: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to respond to Severity 1 incidents within 30 minutes and Severity 2 within four (4) hours for Dedicated customers that provide on-call contact details. We'll include a clear P1 definition and require a named on-call contact for P1 escalations.

4) Maintenance: Planned maintenance will have at least seventy-two (72) hours' notice. We propose a maximum of six (6) planned maintenance events per year that impact Availability. Customers may designate up to two recurring 4-hour weekly blackout windows where planned maintenance will not be scheduled. Emergency maintenance for critical security issues may be performed without prior notice, with a mandatory post-event summary within 24 hours.

Next steps: attached is our redline excerpt "SLA_snippet_redwood_draft_20260530.docx" and a single-sheet summary of the conditional 99.95% appendix. If this looks acceptable, please confirm and I will arrange for DocuSign for the Order Form (link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/IVT-0045-signature). If you prefer a quick sync, I'm available Monday afternoon (PDT) for a 20-minute call to walk through the changes.

Thanks again — goal is to get this to procurement by next Wednesday.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_snippet_redwood_draft_20260530.docx, IVT-99.95%-appendix-onepager.pdf
